correctness.rationale: On the diagonal, the Q_j contributions telescope at coordinate k to ω₁(δ₀−δ_k)x_k, while the Cauchy-dual shift contributes ω₁δ_k x_(k+1); hence the stated bounded two-diagonal restriction is exact. Its coefficient differences from cI+aL tend to zero and are norm limits of finite-rank perturbations. For the backward shift L the open disk has index +1 by the forward-shift right inverse and Neumann series; the exterior is invertible. On the unit circle L−μI is injective but normalized truncations of (μ^j) have residual norm N^(−1/p), so it is not bounded below and its range is not closed, including p=1. For a nonterminating recurrence with μ≠0 the logarithm of the factor modulus equals log|μ|+Re(κ/μ−κ)/j+O(j^(−2)); summation proves exact positive-constant asymptotics and the strong/weak boundary phases. μ=0 is summable directly; μ=1 is constant; the only terminating circle point is −1 when κ is an integer, always on the strict arc. Outside the circle an ℓ^p solution must terminate, exactly at b_j with j<β. Other exterior values are invertible by index zero. For an exterior outlier, the tail block past j is Fredholm of index zero with zero kernel by the same recurrence, so is invertible there; the finite top triangular block has distinct diagonal entries and a simple eigenvalue. This proves algebraic simplicity. Reviewed the exact rational checker as corroboration; the infinite-dimensional proof does not rely on it.

value.rationale: The invariant diagonal is a natural sector of the channel rather than a chosen numerical slice. The same spectral circle has different point spectra depending on the ideal and radial weight: an empty boundary, a born-but-strongly-excluded weak mode, or a strict eigenarc whose endpoints remain weak only. This is additional usable spectral information beyond ordinary spectrum and bounded fixed points, without asserting it about the full noncommutative ideal.
